memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts and bases; the covering of ram skins dyed red and the covering of the other durable leather and the shielding curtain; the ark of the covenant law with its poles and the atonement cover; the table with all its articles and the bread of the Presence." - Exod 39:33-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They did not put it up themselves. They carried everything to Moses and laid it before him.

There is real humility in that. Bezalel and Oholiab had spent months on this work. They could have assembled it and presented a finished tabernacle. Instead, they brought the pieces to the one God had appointed and placed them in his hands.

Every clasp. Every crossbar. Even the ark itself.

That is a picture of how we should hold our work. However skilled we are, however much of ourselves we have poured in, it is not finally ours. We bring it and lay it down.

David prayed it beautifully as Israel gave for the temple: everything comes from You, and we have given You only what comes from Your hand (1 Chron 29:14).

Notice the list is exhaustive. Clasps and crossbars sit in the same sentence as the ark of the covenant. Nothing was too small to bring and nothing too precious to hand over.

Is there something you have been building that you have never actually handed to God? A career, a family, a ministry, a plan? Bring it and lay it down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you built that you have never truly handed over to God?
2. Do you hold your work as an owner or as a steward?
3. What is too precious for you to lay down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, everything I have came from You. I bring my work and lay it before You. Amen.
